signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + CB Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags a dominant divergence as JPY averages +2.300% across 7 pairs while NZD drops -1.280% across 4 pairs, creating an extreme 3.580% spread. JPY strengthens broadly across markets on mounting BoJ rate hike expectations ahead of the 18 Sep meeting, defying its carry deficit. Meanwhile, NZD faces selling pressure with speculative shorts pinned at an extreme LF net of -32,496 (pctl 0, z -2.60). In the rates space, RBNZ at 2.75% versus BoJ at 1.0% provides a 175bp nominal carry advantage to NZD, but capital flows are completely overriding carry to chase the Yen's structural repricing. This bilateral performance gap signals entrenched trend continuation rather than short-term noise. Trade bias: Short NZD/JPY, aligned with dominant G10 cross-asset divergence. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: BoJ leaves policy unadjusted and downplays October hike odds, prompting a sharp carry-driven mean reversion higher.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Trend Breakdown
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 155.97, breaking cleanly below its SMA20 at 159.04, SMA200 at 158.45, and SMA50 at 160.59. The 25-delta Risk Reversals print an extreme put skew of -2.64, showing institutional desks aggressively paying up for downside protection. COT speculative positioning remains heavily short JPY with Leveraged Funds net short -81,619 contracts (pctl 9, z -1.34), creating significant squeeze vulnerability as spot moves lower. The 267bp OIS carry advantage favoring the dollar (SOFR 3.65% vs TONA 0.98%) is failing to anchor spot as market participants price in BoJ tightening. Furthermore, USD/JPY options volatility shows unusual complacency with 1M IV at 7.2% against HV30 of 10.3% (VRP -3.1%), indicating that downside tail hedges remain underpriced relative to realized price action. Trade bias: Short USD/JPY, directional downside continuation below moving average resistance. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — rate hike expected. Risk: Fed pushback against easing expectations alongside firm US labor data driving a swift reclaim of the 158.45 SMA200 level.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Options + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7211, holding firmly above its SMA20 (0.7129) and SMA50 (0.7035) cluster. CFTC data shows institutional Leveraged Funds crowded long at net +53,578 contracts (pctl 95, z +1.92), upper decile positioning reflecting hawkish RBA expectations. Conversely, retail sentiment sits at an extreme 90% short, creating a sharp institutional-versus-retail divergence. While RBA at 4.35% versus Fed at 3.75% provides a 60bp cash carry premium (70bp OIS via AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.65%), 25-delta Risk Reversals post a mild put skew of -0.52. This demonstrates that options markets are hedging spot dips rather than chasing spot higher into multi-month highs. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; crowded positioning caps immediate breakout speed but retail squeeze favors trend continuation. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — on hold at 4.35%. Risk: Leveraged Funds commence broad profit-taking on unexpected Australian disinflation, forcing a drop through the 0.7129 SMA20.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Hawkish Shift
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3532, holding above its SMA50 at 1.3449 and SMA200 at 1.3446 while testing immediate resistance near the SMA20 at 1.3554. Headline comments from BoE Chief Economist Huw Pill advocating for an early hike to 4% inject hawkish policy pressure into the UK yield curve, where the 10Y Gilt prints 5.16% (+39bp over US 10Y). Options markets reflect intense hedging demand with 1M IV at 11.0% versus HV30 of 4.8%, generating an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +6.2%. Leveraged Funds hold net long +56,839 contracts (pctl 96, z +1.58), reflecting a crowded positioning profile that leaves Cable vulnerable to near-term headline volatility despite policy support. Trade bias: Long GBP/USD, supported by BoE rate tightening commentary and sovereign yield support. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep — policy rate 3.75%. Risk: UK macroeconomic data surprises to the downside, causing Gilt yields to collapse back below US Treasuries.
